external.description:
Ukraine was prepared to receive a plane carrying special envoys of former US President Donald Trump, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, but Russian strikes targeted the runways at Boryspil and Kyiv (Zhuliany) airports before their arrival, President Volodymyr Zelensky told reporters, according to Suspilne. 
 Zelensky said both airports technically remained capable of accepting the US delegation despite the strikes. "Ukraine was ready to receive the American plane, the plane with the negotiating delegation. Both Boryspil and Zhuliany could have been used. Russia clearly wanted to send a signal that Ukraine is unsafe, so they struck the runways at both airports," Zelensky said. 
 He added that it was unclear whether Russia would allow a safe air corridor for the flight. According to Zelensky, an alternative was also considered: the delegation could have traveled to Belarus, from where the journey from Homel to Kyiv would have taken about three hours. Ukrainian officials prepared for this scenario and were ready to meet Witkoff and Kushner. 
 However, the US side ultimately chose to travel by train. Zelensky said the entire delegation appreciated this option. He also noted that he had agreed with Trump's representatives on plans for a future visit, suggesting they could fly in next time, leaving the American aircraft in Poland or another country if needed, and continue to Ukraine aboard a Ukrainian presidential plane. 
 Witkoff and Kushner's diplomatic trip to Moscow and Kyiv on September 5–6 was expected to focus on peace negotiations. On September 5, the US envoys arrived in Moscow, where they spent about eight hours before meeting with Vladimir Putin at around 8 p.m. At the start of their conversation, Witkoff described the day as the best of his life, saying he would remember it until retirement. 
 On September 6, the US special representatives traveled by train to Kyiv. By the time of their arrival, Russia had agreed not to strike the Ukrainian capital. Zelensky held three rounds of talks with them in Kyiv, discussing a peace plan, Russia's position, and the air defense systems Ukraine needs to counter Russian ballistic missiles. 
 On September 7, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov made a statement outlining the Kremlin's conditions for ending the war.
external.title: Zelensky says Russian strikes hit airports before Trump envoys visit
